description: Imports Mixpanel product-analytics data: raw exported events, user profiles (engage), cohorts and their members, saved funnel results, and project annotations.

authTierRationale: Both offered credential modes are self-serve static secrets pasted into the config: a Mixpanel Service Account username+secret (plus the numeric project ID) sent as HTTP Basic, or a single project secret that the connector base64-encodes into an `Authorization: Basic` header. There is no OAuth app registration and no refresh token anywhere in the connector — `__main__.py` explicitly constructs the Estuary shim with `oauth2=None`.

unionMisfits.description: This is one logical API with three hostnames/base paths chosen at runtime, not a primary plus a genuinely different sidecar service. Region ('US'|'EU') selects the host prefix, and the Export stream uses an entirely different host family (data.mixpanel.com / data-eu.mixpanel.com) while Annotations swaps the base path to /api/app/projects/ when a project_id is configured. I modelled Export as role 'sidecar' because the schema has no way to say 'one connector, several per-stream hosts', but it is not a second service in the Kafka+schema-registry sense.

The Export endpoint does not paginate at all. It streams newline-delimited JSON for a whole date window in one response (request_kwargs sets stream=True and the connector reassembles records line by line, bailing out on a literal 'terminated early' line). Progress is made only by advancing the from_date/to_date window, capped at 30 days per slice for this stream. Recorded as paginator {'type':'none'}; the real bounding mechanism is the date window, which the PullSpec union has no slot for.

lookback.appliedWhen: only once the stream is caught up to yesterday

unionMisfits.description: The engage-backed paginator is a hybrid the axes cannot express cleanly. Each response body carries `page`, `total` (first page only) and an opaque `session_id`; the next request sends BOTH an incremented `page` number AND that `session_id` back as query parameters. I classified it 'page' because the page number is what advances, but the session_id is a genuine body-sourced opaque cursor riding alongside it. Termination is explicit_total: stop once total <= page_size * (page + 1).

No stream in this connector emits deletes or tombstones, including the two full-refresh ones (cohort_members, annotations). Records are keyed documents reduced last-write-wins by the destination collection, so I used 'merge' throughout; 'snapshot_with_tombstone' would be wrong (nothing is tombstoned) but 'merge' also understates that cohort_members re-reads the entire membership every run and a removed cohort member simply stops being refreshed rather than being deleted.

proposedShape.staleHandling: none — removed source rows are never retracted

unionMisfits.description: Both are parent-scoped streams whose slices come from a second, undeclared HTTP call, and neither parent appears as a bindable stream. cohort_members first reads cohorts/list and iterates the cohorts whose count > 0, sending {"filter_by_cohort": {"id": <cohort id>}} in the POST body. funnels first reads funnels/list and iterates funnel_ids. The PullSpec union has pathPlaceholders for parent scoping via the URL but nothing for parent scoping via a request body or a query param.

There is no schedule anywhere in the connector or in the shared Airbyte-shim ResourceConfig (whose only fields are stream, syncMode, namespace, cursorField). What the connector does have is a self-imposed rate limiter: after every response it sleeps (3600 / reqs_per_hour_limit) seconds minus the response-processing time, with a default limit of 60 requests/hour, overridable by the REQS_PER_HOUR_LIMIT environment variable. That is pacing inside a run, not a schedule between runs, so the schedule fields are left empty.

rateLimit.note: ExportSchema helper sets it to 0 to disable sleeping

unionMisfits.description: The Project Secret mode is neither a plain 'bearer' nor a plain 'basic': the connector base64-encodes the raw project secret itself and sends 'Authorization: Basic <b64(secret)>'. It is basic-auth-shaped on the wire but the user supplies a single opaque value, not a username/password pair, so I used the 'header' variant with the encoding described in the prefix field.

proposedShape.encoding: base64 of the raw field value, applied by the connector

unionMisfits.description: spec.json advertises default 1 while the code's fallback when the key is absent is 30, and three streams then override the user's value outright (Export clamps to at most 30; Funnels and Annotations hard-set 100000 to force a single request). The flat configFields shape cannot express 'declared default disagrees with code default and is per-stream overridden'.

abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Nothing in the connector or in the shared Airbyte-shim ResourceConfig expresses a schedule. The only timing construct is an in-run rate limiter (60 requests/hour by default, REQS_PER_HOUR_LIMIT override) implemented as a post-response sleep, which is pacing within a single run rather than a cadence between runs. Recorded in unionMisfits instead of guessed at.
abstained.streams[*].schedules: Same reason — the resource config has only stream, syncMode, namespace and cursorField; there is no per-binding interval or cron anywhere.
abstained.execution.continuity: mode is 'poll', so continuity is optional. The connector leaves no server-side artifact behind: every stream is a stateless HTTP read and the only persisted state is a client-side cursor. Nothing accrues on Mixpanel's side if we stop, and the only loss on ours would be Mixpanel's own data-retention policy expiring history before we resume, which the connector source does not state. Set null rather than inventing a resume window.
abstained.streams[5].pull.incremental.incrementalP: Engage does not carry its cursor in a dedicated parameter. It bounds each slice with a Mixpanel filter expression in the `where` query param comparing properties["$last_seen"] against slice start/end formatted %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S, then advances state to the slice end. The {param, format} shape cannot represent a two-sided expression filter, and naming `where` as the incrementalParam would be misleading.
abstained.streams[1].pull.snapshot.incrementalPara: cohort_members is full_refresh in discover output and has no cursor_field at all; the parent cohorts sweep is deliberately re-read in full each run because membership changes. The test.flow.yaml binding nonetheless declares syncMode incremental with cursorField last_seen — see FLAG — so I did not assert an incremental parameter.
abstained.streams[4].pull.snapshot.incrementalPara: Annotations sends from_date/to_date, but its date_window_size is hard-set to 100000 days so exactly one all-time window is ever produced, and the stream docstring states it cannot sync incrementally because the annotation date is the annotated-for date, not the created date. Calling from_date an incrementalParam here would misrepresent it as a watermark.
abstained.streams[3].pull.backfill: The Export stream has no separate backfill leg in the code. The same date-window slicer produces both the historical sweep and the ongoing tail; the only difference is the attribution-window lookback, which is applied solely when the stream is already caught up to yesterday. I put the single shape in `incremental` rather than duplicating it into `backfill`.
abstained.discovery: streamMode is static — SourceMixpanel.STREAMS is a fixed list of six classes and the discover snapshot returns exactly those six bindings, so there is no discovery mechanism to describe.
abstained.transports[0].spec.apiVersionPinning (An: The project-scoped Annotations base path (/api/app/projects/) carries no version segment at all, so the connector effectively pins two different API surfaces. Recorded in the transports misfit rather than forced into the single apiVersionPinning string.
abstained.credentialModes[*].appliesToTransport: Both credential modes are applied by a single authenticator constructed once in source.py and handed to every stream, including the Export stream on the data.mixpanel.com host. I marked both 'primary' because the schema requires one value, but they in fact apply to both transports.
